meta.topic: 数值微积分与拟合：最小二乘、数值微分、数值积分、高斯求积

zh: 设数据 $(x_i,y_i)$（$i=1,\dots,m$）和基函数 $\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_n$ 给定，模型取线性组合 $\varphi(x;c)=\sum_{j=1}^{n}c_j\varphi_j(x)$。令 $A_{ij}=\varphi_j(x_i)$，$b=(y_1,\dots,y_m)^{\top}$，$c=(c_1,\dots,c_n)^{\top}$，则残差向量为 $r=b-Ac$，最小二乘问题为 $$\begin{aligned}\min_{c\in\mathbb R^n}Q(c)&=\|Ac-b\|_2^2\\&=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\Big(y_i-\sum_{j=1}^{n}A_{ij}c_j\Big)^2.\end{aligned}$$ 这里只假设数据与基函数已给定，不假设 $A$ 满秩（$n\le m$ 只是列满秩的必要条件）。目标函数 $Q\ge0$，最小值总是存在（$\operatorname{col}(A)$ 是闭子空间），但最小值是否唯一取决于 $A$ 的秩。

固定 $A,b$ 后，$Q$ 是 $c$ 的二次多项式：$$Q(c)=c^{\top}A^{\top}Ac-2c^{\top}A^{\top}b+b^{\top}b.$$ 对 $c_k$ 求偏导得 $$\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial Q}{\partial c_k}&=2\sum_{i=1}^{m}A_{ik}\Big(\sum_{j=1}^{n}A_{ij}c_j-y_i\Big)\\&=2\big(A^{\top}Ac-A^{\top}b\big)_k.\end{aligned}$$ 因 $Q$ 在全空间 $\mathbb R^n$ 可微，任何极小点（全空间的内点）都必须使梯度为零。令梯度为零，得到正规方程 $$A^{\top}Ac=A^{\top}b.$$ 这一步只说明极小点必须满足正规方程，尚未说明解存在且唯一。

设 $A$ 列满秩，即 $Av=0$ 只有零解（这要求 $n\le m$）。对任意 $v
e0$，$$v^{	op}A^{	op}Av=\|Av\|_2^2>0,$$ 故 $A^{	op}A$ 对称正定、可逆，正规方程有唯一解 $$c_*=(A^{	op}A)^{-1}A^{	op}b.$$ 又由 $A^{	op}(b-Ac_*)=0$，令 $c=c_*+d$，则 $Ac-b=Ad-r_*$，且交叉项 $-2r_*^{	op}Ad=0$，故 $$Q(c)=Q(c_*)+(c-c_*)^{	op}A^{	op}A(c-c_*),$$ 右端第二项在 $c
e c_*$ 时严格为正，所以 $c_*$ 是全局严格极小点。若 $A$ 列不满秩，正规方程仍有解，因为 $A^{	op}b\in\operatorname{col}(A^{	op})=\operatorname{col}(A^{	op}A)$；但若 $c_0$ 是一个解、$v
e0$ 满足 $Av=0$，则 $c_0+v$ 也是解且残差相同，故解不唯一。此时应取最小范数解或加正则项。

正规方程等价于 $$A^{\top}(b-Ac_*)=0.$$ 因此残差 $r_*=b-Ac_*$ 与 $A$ 的每一列正交。对任意 $u=Av\in\operatorname{col}(A)$，有 $u^{\top}r_*=v^{\top}A^{\top}r_*=0$。于是 $b=Ac_*+r_*$ 是正交分解，$Ac_*=Pb$ 是 $b$ 在 $\operatorname{col}(A)$ 上的正交投影。由勾股定理 $$\|b\|_2^2=\|Ac_*\|_2^2+\|r_*\|_2^2,$$ 最小化残差等价于最大化投影的长度。特别地，若模型含常数项（$A$ 的某列为 $\mathbf 1$），则 $\mathbf 1^{\top}r_*=0$，即残差之和为零。

取基函数 $1,x$，并设 $x_i$ 不全相等。此时 $$\begin{aligned}A^{\top}A&=\begin{pmatrix}m&\sum_i x_i\\ \sum_i x_i&\sum_i x_i^2\end{pmatrix},\\ A^{\top}b&=\begin{pmatrix}\sum_i y_i\\ \sum_i x_iy_i\end{pmatrix}.\end{aligned}$$ 行列式 $D=m\sum_i x_i^2-\big(\sum_i x_i\big)^2=m\sum_i(x_i-\bar x)^2>0$，故矩阵可逆。Cramer 法则给出 $$\begin{aligned}c_1&=\frac{m\sum_i x_iy_i-\sum_i x_i\sum_i y_i}{D},\\ c_0&=\frac{\sum_i y_i\sum_i x_i^2-\sum_i x_i\sum_i x_iy_i}{D}.\end{aligned}$$ 化简第二式得 $c_0=\bar y-c_1\bar x$，即回归直线必过样本中心 $(\bar x,\bar y)$。

理论上可用 $c_*=(A^{\top}A)^{-1}A^{\top}b$，但数值计算不宜显式求逆。若 $A$ 列满秩，则 $A^{\top}A$ 的奇异值是 $A$ 的奇异值的平方，故 $$\kappa_2(A^{\top}A)=\kappa_2(A)^2,$$ 条件数被平方，误差放大因子由 $\kappa_2(A)$ 变为 $\kappa_2(A)^2$，可能使丢失的有效数字位数大约翻倍。改用 Householder QR 分解 $A=QR$，其中 $Q$ 是 $m\times n$ 列正交矩阵、$R$ 是 $n\times n$ 可逆上三角矩阵。则 $$\|Ac-b\|_2^2=\|Rc-Q^{\top}b\|_2^2+\|(I-QQ^{\top})b\|_2^2,$$ 第二项与 $c$ 无关，最小化只需解上三角方程 $Rc=Q^{\top}b$ 并回代，既不形成 $A^{\top}A$ 也不求逆。若 $A$ 秩亏，则用 SVD（或完全正交分解）求最小范数解；带列主元的 QR 可用于判定数值秩和稳定求解。
en: Let data $(x_i,y_i)$ ($i=1,\dots,m$) and basis functions $\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_n$ be given, and take the model $\varphi(x;c)=\sum_{j=1}^{n}c_j\varphi_j(x)$. Set $A_{ij}=\varphi_j(x_i)$, $b=(y_1,\dots,y_m)^{\top}$ and $c=(c_1,\dots,c_n)^{\top}$. The residual vector is $r=b-Ac$, and the least squares problem is $$\begin{aligned}\min_{c\in\mathbb R^n}Q(c)&=\|Ac-b\|_2^2\\&=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\Big(y_i-\sum_{j=1}^{n}A_{ij}c_j\Big)^2.\end{aligned}$$ We assume only that the data and basis functions are given; $A$ is not assumed to have full rank ($n\le m$ is merely necessary for full column rank). The objective satisfies $Q\ge0$; a minimizer always exists because $\operatorname{col}(A)$ is a closed subspace, but its uniqueness depends on the rank of $A$.

Once $A$ and $b$ are fixed, $Q$ is a quadratic polynomial in $c$: $$Q(c)=c^{\top}A^{\top}Ac-2c^{\top}A^{\top}b+b^{\top}b.$$ Differentiating with respect to $c_k$ gives $$\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial Q}{\partial c_k}&=2\sum_{i=1}^{m}A_{ik}\Big(\sum_{j=1}^{n}A_{ij}c_j-y_i\Big)\\&=2\big(A^{\top}Ac-A^{\top}b\big)_k.\end{aligned}$$ Since $Q$ is differentiable on all of $\mathbb R^n$, every minimizer (an interior point of the whole space) must have zero gradient. Setting the gradient to zero gives the normal equations $$A^{\top}Ac=A^{\top}b.$$ This step only shows that any minimizer must satisfy them; existence and uniqueness are not yet established.

Assume $A$ has full column rank, that is, $Av=0$ only for $v=0$ (this requires $n\le m$). For every $v
e0$, $$v^{	op}A^{	op}Av=\|Av\|_2^2>0,$$ so $A^{	op}A$ is symmetric positive definite and invertible, and the normal equations have the unique solution $$c_*=(A^{	op}A)^{-1}A^{	op}b.$$ Moreover, $A^{	op}(b-Ac_*)=0$. Writing $c=c_*+d$ gives $Ac-b=Ad-r_*$, and the cross term $-2r_*^{	op}Ad$ vanishes, so $$Q(c)=Q(c_*)+(c-c_*)^{	op}A^{	op}A(c-c_*),$$ and the second term on the right is strictly positive whenever $c
e c_*$. Hence $c_*$ is the unique global minimizer. If $A$ is rank deficient, the normal equations are still consistent, since $A^{	op}b\in\operatorname{col}(A^{	op})=\operatorname{col}(A^{	op}A)$. But if $c_0$ is one solution and $v
e0$ satisfies $Av=0$, then $c_0+v$ is also a solution with the same residual, so the solution is not unique. One then takes the minimum-norm solution or adds a regularization term.

The normal equations are equivalent to $$A^{\top}(b-Ac_*)=0.$$ Therefore the residual $r_*=b-Ac_*$ is orthogonal to every column of $A$. For any $u=Av\in\operatorname{col}(A)$, $$u^{\top}r_*=v^{\top}A^{\top}r_*=0.$$ Thus $b=Ac_*+r_*$ is an orthogonal decomposition, and $Ac_*=Pb$ is the orthogonal projection of $b$ onto $\operatorname{col}(A)$. Pythagoras' theorem gives $$\|b\|_2^2=\|Ac_*\|_2^2+\|r_*\|_2^2,$$ so minimizing the residual is equivalent to maximizing the length of the projection. In particular, if the model contains an intercept (one column of $A$ is $\mathbf 1$), then $\mathbf 1^{\top}r_*=0$, i.e. the residuals sum to zero.

Take the basis functions $1,x$ and suppose the $x_i$ are not all equal. Then $$\begin{aligned}A^{\top}A&=\begin{pmatrix}m&\sum_i x_i\\ \sum_i x_i&\sum_i x_i^2\end{pmatrix},\\ A^{\top}b&=\begin{pmatrix}\sum_i y_i\\ \sum_i x_iy_i\end{pmatrix}.\end{aligned}$$ Its determinant is $D=m\sum_i x_i^2-\big(\sum_i x_i\big)^2=m\sum_i(x_i-\bar x)^2>0$, so the matrix is invertible. Cramer's rule gives $$\begin{aligned}c_1&=\frac{m\sum_i x_iy_i-\sum_i x_i\sum_i y_i}{D},\\ c_0&=\frac{\sum_i y_i\sum_i x_i^2-\sum_i x_i\sum_i x_iy_i}{D}.\end{aligned}$$ Simplifying the second expression yields $c_0=\bar y-c_1\bar x$, so the regression line passes through the sample mean $(\bar x,\bar y)$.

In theory one can use $c_*=(A^{\top}A)^{-1}A^{\top}b$, but explicit inversion is inappropriate in numerical computation. If $A$ has full column rank, the singular values of $A^{\top}A$ are the squares of those of $A$, hence $$\kappa_2(A^{\top}A)=\kappa_2(A)^2,$$ so the condition number is squared: the error amplification factor changes from $\kappa_2(A)$ to $\kappa_2(A)^2$, and the number of digits lost may roughly double. Instead, use a Householder QR factorization $A=QR$, where $Q$ is $m\times n$ with orthonormal columns and $R$ is $n\times n$, upper triangular and invertible. Then $$\|Ac-b\|_2^2=\|Rc-Q^{\top}b\|_2^2+\|(I-QQ^{\top})b\|_2^2,$$ and the second term is independent of $c$. The minimization therefore reduces to solving the upper triangular system $Rc=Q^{\top}b$ by back substitution, without forming $A^{\top}A$ or inverting a matrix. If $A$ is rank deficient, use the SVD (or a complete orthogonal decomposition) to obtain the minimum-norm solution; column-pivoted QR is useful for determining the numerical rank and for stable solving.

zh: 设 $f\in C^2$ 在以 $x$ 与 $x+h$ 为端点的闭区间上，$h\ne0$。带 Lagrange 余项的 Taylor 公式给出 $$f(x+h)=f(x)+hf'(x)+\frac{h^2}{2}f''(\xi_+),$$ 其中 $\xi_+$ 介于 $x$ 与 $x+h$ 之间。移项并除以 $h$：$$D_+(h)=\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}=f'(x)+\frac{h}{2}f''(\xi_+).$$ 故前向差商的截断误差为 $O(h)$；若 $|f''|\le M$，则 $|D_+(h)-f'(x)|\le M|h|/2$。同理，后向差商满足 $$D_-(h)=\frac{f(x)-f(x-h)}{h}=f'(x)-\frac{h}{2}f''(\xi_-),$$ 误差同样是 $O(h)$。

设 $f\in C^3$。把 $x+h$ 与 $x-h$ 处的 Taylor 展开写到三阶：$$f(x+h)=f+hf'+\frac{h^2}{2}f''+\frac{h^3}{6}f'''(\xi_+),$$ $$f(x-h)=f-hf'+\frac{h^2}{2}f''-\frac{h^3}{6}f'''(\xi_-).$$ 两式相减，偶次项抵消：$$f(x+h)-f(x-h)=2hf'+\frac{h^3}{6}\big[f'''(\xi_+)+f'''(\xi_-)\big].$$ 因 $f'''$ 连续，由介值定理存在 $\xi$ 使方括号等于 $2f'''(\xi)$。除以 $2h$ 得 $$D_c(h)=\frac{f(x+h)-f(x-h)}{2h}=f'(x)+\frac{h^2}{6}f'''(\xi).$$ 因此中心差商的截断误差为 $O(h^2)$，比单侧差商高一阶；代价是要求 $f\in C^3$ 且 $x\pm h$ 都在定义域内。

设 $f\in C^4$。把上述两式相加，奇次项抵消：$$f(x+h)+f(x-h)=2f(x)+h^2f''(x)+\frac{h^4}{24}\big[f^{(4)}(\eta_+)+f^{(4)}(\eta_-)\big].$$ 由 $f^{(4)}$ 的连续性并用介值定理，存在 $\eta$ 使方括号等于 $2f^{(4)}(\eta)$。于是 $$D_2(h)=\frac{f(x+h)-2f(x)+f(x-h)}{h^2}=f''(x)+\frac{h^2}{12}f^{(4)}(\eta).$$ 故二阶中心差商也是 $O(h^2)$，但它需要四阶光滑性；它也可看作对步长 $h/2$ 的两个一阶中心差商再作一次差商。

实际计算只能得到带舍入误差的函数值 $\hat f(x\pm h)=f(x\pm h)(1+\delta_\pm)$，$|\delta_\pm|\le u$，其中 $u$ 是机器精度（双精度约 $2.2\times10^{-16}$）。中心差商的总误差由截断项 $\frac{h^2}{6}f'''(\xi)$ 与舍入项 $$\frac{[\hat f(x+h)-f(x+h)]-[\hat f(x-h)-f(x-h)]}{2h}$$ 组成；后者绝对值不超过约 $u|f|/h$，更一般地记为 $\varepsilon/h$，其中 $\varepsilon$ 是函数值的绝对误差水平。因此总误差模型为 $$E(h)\approx\frac{Mh^2}{6}+\frac{\varepsilon}{h},\qquad M=\max|f'''|.$$ 求导得 $E'(h)=\frac{Mh}{3}-\frac{\varepsilon}{h^2}$，令其为零得 $$h_*=\Big(\frac{3\varepsilon}{M}\Big)^{1/3},$$ 且 $E''(h)=M/3+2\varepsilon/h^3>0$，故这是极小点。结论：$h$ 并非越小越好；舍入误差随 $h$ 减小按 $1/h$ 增大，双精度下 $M\sim1$ 时 $h_*\sim10^{-5}$。

设 $h>0$。中心公式要求 $x-h$ 与 $x+h$ 都在定义域内，因此在端点只能用单侧公式。在左端点 $a$ 用 $f(a),f(a+h),f(a+2h)$（要求 $a+2h\le b$）作二次插值并求导，得到 $$\begin{aligned}D_+^{(2)}(a)&=\frac{-3f(a)+4f(a+h)-f(a+2h)}{2h}\\&=f'(a)-\frac{h^2}{3}f'''(\xi),\end{aligned}$$ 其中 $\xi\in(a,a+2h)$，故仍是 $O(h^2)$。在右端点 $b$ 同理，用 $f(b),f(b-h),f(b-2h)$（要求 $b-2h\ge a$）：$$D_-^{(2)}(b)=\frac{3f(b)-4f(b-h)+f(b-2h)}{2h}=f'(b)-\frac{h^2}{3}f'''(\eta),$$ 其中 $\eta\in(b-2h,b)$。若在端点强行使用中心公式，就会用到定义域外的函数值；若改用一阶单侧差商，精度则降为 $O(h)$。

若 $f\in C^5$，中心差商有展开 $$\begin{aligned}D(h)&=f'(x)+c_2h^2+c_4h^4+o(h^4),\\ c_2&=\frac{f'''(x)}{6},\qquad c_4=\frac{f^{(5)}(x)}{120}.\end{aligned}$$ 于是 $$D(h/2)=f'(x)+\frac{c_2h^2}{4}+\frac{c_4h^4}{16}+o(h^4).$$ 用组合 $\frac{4D(h/2)-D(h)}{3}$ 消去 $h^2$ 项：$$\frac{4D(h/2)-D(h)}{3}=f'(x)-\frac{c_4h^4}{4}+o(h^4)=f'(x)+O(h^4).$$ 这就是 Richardson 外推。条件是 $f$ 足够光滑（$C^5$ 已能保证 $O(h^4)$ 余项）；它不能消除舍入误差，组合后的舍入仍约为 $\varepsilon/h$，所以外推并不能让最优步长无限变小。
en: Let $f\in C^2$ on the closed interval with endpoints $x$ and $x+h$, $h\ne0$. Taylor's formula with Lagrange remainder gives $$f(x+h)=f(x)+hf'(x)+\frac{h^2}{2}f''(\xi_+),$$ where $\xi_+$ lies between $x$ and $x+h$. Rearranging and dividing by $h$ gives $$D_+(h)=\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}=f'(x)+\frac{h}{2}f''(\xi_+).$$ Hence the forward difference has truncation error $O(h)$; if $|f''|\le M$, then $|D_+(h)-f'(x)|\le M|h|/2$. Similarly, the backward difference satisfies $$D_-(h)=\frac{f(x)-f(x-h)}{h}=f'(x)-\frac{h}{2}f''(\xi_-),$$ and is also $O(h)$.

Let $f\in C^3$. Expand at $x+h$ and $x-h$ through third order: $$f(x+h)=f+hf'+\frac{h^2}{2}f''+\frac{h^3}{6}f'''(\xi_+),$$ $$f(x-h)=f-hf'+\frac{h^2}{2}f''-\frac{h^3}{6}f'''(\xi_-).$$ Subtracting cancels the even-order terms: $$f(x+h)-f(x-h)=2hf'+\frac{h^3}{6}\big[f'''(\xi_+)+f'''(\xi_-)\big].$$ Since $f'''$ is continuous, the intermediate value theorem gives some $\xi$ for which the bracket equals $2f'''(\xi)$. Dividing by $2h$ yields $$D_c(h)=\frac{f(x+h)-f(x-h)}{2h}=f'(x)+\frac{h^2}{6}f'''(\xi).$$ Therefore the central difference has truncation error $O(h^2)$, one order better than the one-sided formulas; the price is the hypothesis $f\in C^3$ and the need for $x\pm h$ to lie in the domain.

Let $f\in C^4$. Adding the two expansions cancels the odd-order terms: $$f(x+h)+f(x-h)=2f(x)+h^2f''(x)+\frac{h^4}{24}\big[f^{(4)}(\eta_+)+f^{(4)}(\eta_-)\big].$$ By continuity of $f^{(4)}$ and the intermediate value theorem, some $\eta$ makes the bracket equal $2f^{(4)}(\eta)$. Hence $$D_2(h)=\frac{f(x+h)-2f(x)+f(x-h)}{h^2}=f''(x)+\frac{h^2}{12}f^{(4)}(\eta).$$ Thus the central second difference is also $O(h^2)$, but it requires fourth-order smoothness; it can also be viewed as one more difference quotient applied to two first central differences with step $h/2$.

In actual computation one obtains only function values with rounding error $\hat f(x\pm h)=f(x\pm h)(1+\delta_\pm)$, $|\delta_\pm|\le u$, where $u$ is the machine precision (about $2.2\times10^{-16}$ in double precision). The total error of the central difference consists of the truncation term $\frac{h^2}{6}f'''(\xi)$ and the rounding term $$\frac{[\hat f(x+h)-f(x+h)]-[\hat f(x-h)-f(x-h)]}{2h},$$ whose magnitude is at most about $u|f|/h$, or more generally $\varepsilon/h$, where $\varepsilon$ is the absolute error level of the function values. Hence the total error model is $$E(h)\approx\frac{Mh^2}{6}+\frac{\varepsilon}{h},\qquad M=\max|f'''|.$$ Differentiating gives $E'(h)=\frac{Mh}{3}-\frac{\varepsilon}{h^2}$; setting it to zero yields $$h_*=\Big(\frac{3\varepsilon}{M}\Big)^{1/3},$$ and $E''(h)=M/3+2\varepsilon/h^3>0$, so this is a minimum. Conclusion: $h$ is not the smaller the better; the rounding error grows like $1/h$ as $h$ decreases, and in double precision with $M\sim1$, $h_*\sim10^{-5}$.

Assume $h>0$. The central formula requires both $x-h$ and $x+h$ to lie in the domain, so at endpoints one must use one-sided formulas. At the left endpoint $a$, provided $a+2h\le b$, interpolate $f(a),f(a+h),f(a+2h)$ by a quadratic and differentiate: $$\begin{aligned}D_+^{(2)}(a)&=\frac{-3f(a)+4f(a+h)-f(a+2h)}{2h}\\&=f'(a)-\frac{h^2}{3}f'''(\xi),\end{aligned}$$ where $\xi\in(a,a+2h)$; the error is still $O(h^2)$. At the right endpoint $b$, provided $b-2h\ge a$, similarly, using $f(b),f(b-h),f(b-2h)$: $$D_-^{(2)}(b)=\frac{3f(b)-4f(b-h)+f(b-2h)}{2h}=f'(b)-\frac{h^2}{3}f'''(\eta),$$ where $\eta\in(b-2h,b)$. If one insists on the central formula at an endpoint, values outside the domain are needed; if one uses a first-order one-sided difference instead, the accuracy drops to $O(h)$.

If $f\in C^5$, the central difference has the expansion $$\begin{aligned}D(h)&=f'(x)+c_2h^2+c_4h^4+o(h^4),\\ c_2&=\frac{f'''(x)}{6},\qquad c_4=\frac{f^{(5)}(x)}{120}.\end{aligned}$$ Thus $$D(h/2)=f'(x)+\frac{c_2h^2}{4}+\frac{c_4h^4}{16}+o(h^4).$$ The combination $\frac{4D(h/2)-D(h)}{3}$ cancels the $h^2$ term: $$\frac{4D(h/2)-D(h)}{3}=f'(x)-\frac{c_4h^4}{4}+o(h^4)=f'(x)+O(h^4).$$ This is Richardson extrapolation. The hypothesis is sufficient smoothness ($C^5$ already ensures an $O(h^4)$ remainder); it cannot remove rounding error, since the combined rounding remains of order $\varepsilon/h$, so extrapolation does not allow the optimal step to become arbitrarily small.

zh: 设 $f\in C^2[a,b]$，在 $[a,b]$ 上取线性插值 $$p_1(x)=f(a)\frac{b-x}{b-a}+f(b)\frac{x-a}{b-a}.$$ 插值余项为 $$f(x)-p_1(x)=\frac{f''(\xi_x)}{2}(x-a)(x-b).$$ 因为 $(x-a)(x-b)\le0$ 在 $[a,b]$ 上不变号，且 $f''$ 连续，积分后用加权中值定理：$$\begin{aligned}\int_a^b f(x)\,dx-\int_a^b p_1(x)\,dx&=\frac12\int_a^b f''(\xi_x)(x-a)(x-b)\,dx\\&=-\frac{(b-a)^3}{12}f''(\xi).\end{aligned}$$ 而 $\int_a^b p_1(x)\,dx=\frac{b-a}{2}[f(a)+f(b)]=T$。故梯形公式的余项（真值减近似）为 $$I-T=-\frac{(b-a)^3}{12}f''(\xi).$$ 当 $f''>0$ 时 $I-T<0$，即梯形公式高估积分。

把 $[a,b]$ 等分为 $n$ 段，$h=(b-a)/n$，$x_i=a+ih$，则 $$T_n=\frac{h}{2}\Big[f(a)+2\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}f(x_i)+f(b)\Big].$$ 对每段 $[x_{i-1},x_i]$ 用第 1 步，得 $I_i-T_i=-\frac{h^3}{12}f''(\xi_i)$。相加得 $$I-T_n=-\frac{h^3}{12}\sum_{i=1}^{n}f''(\xi_i)=-\frac{nh^3}{12}f''(\xi),$$ 最后一步用 $f''$ 的连续性与加权中值定理（各系数同号）。由 $nh=b-a$，$$I-T_n=-\frac{(b-a)h^2}{12}f''(\xi)=-\frac{(b-a)^3}{12n^2}f''(\xi).$$ 故复化梯形误差为 $O(h^2)$；$n$ 加倍时误差约变为原来的 $1/4$。

设 $n$ 为偶数，$h=(b-a)/n$，把 $[a,b]$ 分成 $n/2$ 个长度为 $2h$ 的片。逐片用第 3 步的公式并求和，得 $$S_n=\frac{h}{3}\Big[f(a)+4\sum_{i\ \text{odd}}f(x_i)+2\sum_{i\ \text{even}}f(x_i)+f(b)\Big],$$ 其中 $i=1,\dots,n-1$。每片的误差为 $I_k-S_k=-\frac{h^5}{90}f^{(4)}(\xi_k)$。由 $f^{(4)}$ 的连续性与加权中值定理，相加得 $$\begin{aligned}I-S_n&=-\frac{h^5}{90}\sum_{k=1}^{n/2}f^{(4)}(\xi_k)\\&=-\frac{(n/2)h^5}{90}f^{(4)}(\xi)\\&=-\frac{(b-a)h^4}{180}f^{(4)}(\xi).\end{aligned}$$ 故复化 Simpson 的余项为 $O(h^4)$，$n$ 加倍时误差约降为原来的 $1/16$。$n$ 必须为偶数，因为每片抛物线覆盖两个子区间；$f\in C^4$ 是误差公式的前提。

代数精度定义为对所有次数不超过 $k$ 的多项式都精确成立的最大 $k$。梯形公式对 $f=1,x$ 精确（线性插值本身对这些函数精确），但对 $f=x^2$ 在 $[0,1]$ 上，$$\int_0^1x^2\,dx=\frac13,\qquad T=\frac12(0+1)=\frac12,$$ 误差 $I-T=-\frac16\ne0$，故其代数精度为 $1$。Simpson 公式在第 3 步已证对三次多项式精确；但对 $f=x^4$ 在 $[-1,1]$ 上，$$\int_{-1}^{1}x^4\,dx=\frac25,\qquad S=\frac13[1+4\cdot0+1]=\frac23,$$ 误差 $I-S=-\frac{4}{15}\ne0$，故其代数精度恰为 $3$。精度 $3$ 高于二次插值的次数 $2$，原因是节点对称使三次项的误差自动抵消。

第 2、4 步的误差公式都要求 $f''$ 或 $f^{(4)}$ 在 $[a,b]$ 上有界且连续。若 $f$ 在内部某点间断或不可微，应先在该点拆分积分，再在每段光滑子区间上使用复化公式；跨过间断点套公式得不到通常的误差阶。若端点有代数奇性，例如 $\int_0^1x^{1/2}\,dx$，则 $f''=-\frac14x^{-3/2}$ 无界，$O(h^2)$ 估计失效。第一片误差为 $$\int_0^h\sqrt{x}\,dx-\frac h2\sqrt h=\frac16h^{3/2}.$$ 对第 $k$ 片（$k\ge2$；第一片已单独计算）靠近 $0$ 的区间，$f''\sim(kh)^{-3/2}$，该片误差约为 $h^3(kh)^{-3/2}=h^{3/2}k^{-3/2}$；而 $\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-3/2}$ 收敛，故靠近 $0$ 的片合计 $O(h^{3/2})$，远离 $0$ 的光滑片合计 $O(h^2)$。因此复化梯形总误差为 $O(h^{3/2})=O(n^{-3/2})$。此时可作变量代换 $x=t^2$（$dx=2t\,dt$）把被积函数化为光滑的 $2t^2$，或使用分级网格、带权高斯公式。另需注意：高阶 Newton–Cotes 公式可能出现负权重，数值上不稳定，实际更常用低阶复化公式或高斯公式。
en: Let $f\in C^2[a,b]$ and let $p_1$ be the linear interpolant $$p_1(x)=f(a)\frac{b-x}{b-a}+f(b)\frac{x-a}{b-a}.$$ The interpolation remainder is $$f(x)-p_1(x)=\frac{f''(\xi_x)}{2}(x-a)(x-b).$$ Since $(x-a)(x-b)\le0$ does not change sign on $[a,b]$ and $f''$ is continuous, integrating and applying the weighted mean value theorem gives $$\begin{aligned}\int_a^b f(x)\,dx-\int_a^b p_1(x)\,dx&=\frac12\int_a^b f''(\xi_x)(x-a)(x-b)\,dx\\&=-\frac{(b-a)^3}{12}f''(\xi).\end{aligned}$$ Moreover $\int_a^b p_1(x)\,dx=\frac{b-a}{2}[f(a)+f(b)]=T$. Hence the trapezoidal remainder (true value minus approximation) is $$I-T=-\frac{(b-a)^3}{12}f''(\xi).$$ When $f''>0$, $I-T<0$, so the trapezoidal rule overestimates the integral.

Divide $[a,b]$ into $n$ equal panels, $h=(b-a)/n$, $x_i=a+ih$. Then $$T_n=\frac{h}{2}\Big[f(a)+2\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}f(x_i)+f(b)\Big].$$ Applying Step 1 on each panel $[x_{i-1},x_i]$ gives $I_i-T_i=-\frac{h^3}{12}f''(\xi_i)$. Summing, $$I-T_n=-\frac{h^3}{12}\sum_{i=1}^{n}f''(\xi_i)=-\frac{nh^3}{12}f''(\xi),$$ where the last step uses continuity of $f''$ and the weighted mean value theorem (all coefficients have the same sign). Since $nh=b-a$, $$I-T_n=-\frac{(b-a)h^2}{12}f''(\xi)=-\frac{(b-a)^3}{12n^2}f''(\xi).$$ Thus the composite trapezoidal error is $O(h^2)$; doubling $n$ reduces it by about a factor of $4$.

Let $f\in C^4[x_0,x_2]$, let $x_1$ be the midpoint and $h=x_1-x_0=x_2-x_1$. Integrating the quadratic interpolant $p_2$ through the three points gives $$\int_{x_0}^{x_2}p_2(x)\,dx=\frac{h}{3}[f_0+4f_1+f_2]=S.$$ To obtain the remainder, use instead the cubic Hermite interpolant $p_3$ satisfying $p_3(x_i)=f(x_i)$ for $i=0,1,2$ and $p_3'(x_1)=f'(x_1)$. Since $p_3$ agrees with $f$ at the three nodes, $S(f)=S(p_3)$; direct verification on $[-h,h]$ (and by translation on any panel) gives $S(1)=2h$, $S(x)=0$, $S(x^2)=\frac{2h^3}{3}$ and $S(x^3)=0$, which equal $\int_{-h}^{h}1\,dx,\ \int_{-h}^{h}x\,dx,\ \int_{-h}^{h}x^2\,dx,\ \int_{-h}^{h}x^3\,dx$, respectively. Hence $S(p_3)=I(p_3)$. The Hermite remainder is $$f(x)-p_3(x)=\frac{f^{(4)}(\xi_x)}{4!}(x-x_0)(x-x_1)^2(x-x_2).$$ With $t=(x-x_1)/h$, $(x-x_0)(x-x_1)^2(x-x_2)=h^4t^2(t^2-1)$, and $$\int_{-1}^{1}h^4t^2(t^2-1)\,h\,dt=h^5\Big(\frac25-\frac23\Big)=-\frac{4h^5}{15}.$$ By the weighted mean value theorem (this factor does not change sign on $[x_0,x_2]$), $$I-S=\frac{1}{24}\Big(-\frac{4h^5}{15}\Big)f^{(4)}(\xi)=-\frac{h^5}{90}f^{(4)}(\xi).$$ The hypothesis $f\in C^4$ cannot be dropped.

Let $n$ be even, $h=(b-a)/n$, and split $[a,b]$ into $n/2$ panels of length $2h$. Summing the panel rule from Step 3 gives $$S_n=\frac{h}{3}\Big[f(a)+4\sum_{i\ \text{odd}}f(x_i)+2\sum_{i\ \text{even}}f(x_i)+f(b)\Big],$$ where $i=1,\dots,n-1$. The error on each panel is $I_k-S_k=-\frac{h^5}{90}f^{(4)}(\xi_k)$. By continuity of $f^{(4)}$ and the weighted mean value theorem, summing gives $$\begin{aligned}I-S_n&=-\frac{h^5}{90}\sum_{k=1}^{n/2}f^{(4)}(\xi_k)\\&=-\frac{(n/2)h^5}{90}f^{(4)}(\xi)\\&=-\frac{(b-a)h^4}{180}f^{(4)}(\xi).\end{aligned}$$ Thus the composite Simpson remainder is $O(h^4)$, and doubling $n$ reduces the error by about a factor of $16$. The number $n$ must be even because each parabolic panel covers two subintervals; $f\in C^4$ is required by the error formula.

The degree of precision is the largest $k$ such that the rule is exact for every polynomial of degree at most $k$. The trapezoidal rule is exact for $f=1,x$ (the linear interpolant is exact for them), but for $f=x^2$ on $[0,1]$, $$\int_0^1x^2\,dx=\frac13,\qquad T=\frac12(0+1)=\frac12,$$ with error $I-T=-\frac16\ne0$; hence its degree is $1$. For Simpson's rule, Step 3 already proves exactness for cubics; but for $f=x^4$ on $[-1,1]$, $$\int_{-1}^{1}x^4\,dx=\frac25,\qquad S=\frac13[1+4\cdot0+1]=\frac23,$$ with error $I-S=-\frac{4}{15}\ne0$; hence its degree is exactly $3$. The degree $3$ exceeds the degree $2$ of the interpolating polynomial because the symmetry of the nodes makes the cubic error cancel automatically.

The error formulas in Steps 2 and 4 require $f''$ or $f^{(4)}$ to be bounded and continuous on $[a,b]$. If $f$ has an interior discontinuity or a point where it is not differentiable, split the integral there and apply the composite rules on each smooth subinterval; applying a formula across a discontinuity does not give the usual error order. If there is an algebraic singularity at an endpoint, for example $\int_0^1x^{1/2}\,dx$, then $f''=-\frac14x^{-3/2}$ is unbounded and the $O(h^2)$ estimate fails. The first panel contributes $$\int_0^h\sqrt{x}\,dx-\frac h2\sqrt h=\frac16h^{3/2}.$$ For the $k$-th panel ($k\ge2$; the first panel was computed separately) near $0$, $f''\sim(kh)^{-3/2}$, so its error is about $h^3(kh)^{-3/2}=h^{3/2}k^{-3/2}$; since $\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-3/2}$ converges, the panels near $0$ contribute $O(h^{3/2})$ in total, while the smooth panels away from $0$ contribute $O(h^2)$. Hence the composite trapezoidal error is $O(h^{3/2})=O(n^{-3/2})$. One may then substitute $x=t^2$ ($dx=2t\,dt$), which makes the integrand the smooth function $2t^2$, or use a graded mesh or a weighted Gaussian rule. Note also that high-order Newton–Cotes rules may have negative weights and are numerically unstable; in practice low-order composite rules or Gaussian rules are preferred.

zh: 设 $w$ 在 $(a,b)$ 上连续、非负且不恒为零（更一般地，只需 $w\ge0$ 且在某个正测度集上为正）。求积公式为 $$\int_a^b w(x)f(x)\,dx\approx\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_if(x_i),$$ 节点 $x_i$ 互异。若该公式对所有次数不超过 $d$ 的多项式精确，取 $$p(x)=\prod_{i=1}^{n}(x-x_i)^2,$$ 则 $\deg p=2n$，$p(x_i)=0$，故右端为 $0$；但 $p\ge0$ 且只在有限个点为零，而 $w$ 在正测度集上为正，所以 $\int_a^bw(x)p(x)\,dx>0$。矛盾说明 $d\le2n-1$：任何 $n$ 点公式的代数精度都不可能达到 $2n$。

设 $w$ 的各阶矩 $\int_a^b w(x)x^k\,dx$ 有限，$\{p_k\}$ 是关于 $w$ 的首一正交多项式，$\deg p_k=k$，且 $\int_a^bw p_kp_l=0$（$k\ne l$）；这样的多项式可由 Gram–Schmidt 从 $1,x,x^2,\dots$ 得到。对正权，$p_n$ 的 $n$ 个零点互异且全部位于 $(a,b)$ 内，取它们为节点 $x_i$。对任意 $\deg f\le2n-1$，作带余除法 $$f(x)=q(x)p_n(x)+r(x),\qquad \deg q,\deg r\le n-1.$$ 由正交性 $\int_a^bw qp_n=0$，故 $\int_a^bwf=\int_a^bwr$。令 $A_i=\int_a^bw(x)\ell_i(x)\,dx$，其中 $\ell_i$ 是节点上的 Lagrange 基函数。因 $r=\sum_ir(x_i)\ell_i$，有 $\sum_iA_ir(x_i)=\int_a^bwr$；又 $p_n(x_i)=0$ 给出 $f(x_i)=r(x_i)$，所以 $\sum_iA_if(x_i)=\int_a^bwf$。故公式对一切 $\deg f\le2n-1$ 精确；结合第 1 步，$2n-1$ 就是最大值。反之，若某个 $n$ 点公式也达到 $2n-1$，令 $P(x)=\prod_i(x-x_i)$；对任意 $\deg q\le n-1$，$qP$ 的次数不超过 $2n-1$ 且在节点处为零，故 $\int_a^bw qP=0$。于是 $P$ 与所有次数不超过 $n-1$ 的多项式正交，必为 $p_n$ 的常数倍；又 $P,p_n$ 都是首一多项式，故 $P=p_n$，节点就是 $p_n$ 的零点。因此达到上界的节点选择唯一（不计次序）。

取 $[a,b]=[-1,1]$、$w=1$，正交多项式为 Legendre 多项式 $P_n$，满足 $P_0=1$、$P_1=x$ 及递推 $$(n+1)P_{n+1}(x)=(2n+1)xP_n(x)-nP_{n-1}(x),\qquad P_n(1)=1.$$ 取 $P_n$ 的零点 $x_i$ 为节点（首一化不改变零点）。由 Christoffel–Darboux 恒等式可得 $$\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{P_n(x)}{x-x_i}\,dx=\frac{2}{(1-x_i^2)P_n'(x_i)},$$ 而 $\ell_i(x)=\frac{P_n(x)}{P_n'(x_i)(x-x_i)}$，故 $$A_i=\int_{-1}^{1}\ell_i(x)\,dx=\frac{2}{(1-x_i^2)[P_n'(x_i)]^2}.$$ 这里用了恒等式 $(1-x^2)P_n'(x)=n[P_{n-1}(x)-xP_n(x)]$，在零点处化为 $(1-x_i^2)P_n'(x_i)=nP_{n-1}(x_i)$。因为 $x_i\in(-1,1)$，有 $1-x_i^2>0$ 且 $[P_n'(x_i)]^2>0$，所以 $A_i>0$；又常数 $1$ 被精确积分，$\sum_iA_i=\int_{-1}^1 1\,dx=2$。

低阶公式可直接核对：$n=1$ 时 $P_1=x$，节点 $0$，$A_1=\frac{2}{1\cdot1}=2$，即中点公式；$n=2$ 时 $P_2=\frac12(3x^2-1)$，节点 $\pm\frac1{\sqrt3}$，$P_2'=3x$，$A_i=\frac{2}{(1-\frac13)\cdot3}=1$；$n=3$ 时 $P_3=\frac12(5x^3-3x)$，节点 $0,\pm\sqrt{\frac35}$，权重依次为 $\frac89,\frac59,\frac59$。验证精度：$n=2$ 对 $x^2$ 有 $\sum_iA_ix_i^2=2\cdot\frac13=\frac23=\int_{-1}^1x^2dx$，对 $x^4$ 有 $\sum_iA_ix_i^4=2\cdot\frac19=\frac29\ne\frac25$，故其精度恰为 $2n-1=3$。$n=3$ 对 $x^4$ 有 $2\cdot\frac59\cdot\frac{9}{25}=\frac25$，与积分一致，因为 $4\le2n-1=5$。

对一般区间 $[a,b]$，令 $$x=\frac{a+b}{2}+\frac{b-a}{2}t,\qquad t\in[-1,1],\qquad dx=\frac{b-a}{2}\,dt.$$ 则 $$\int_a^bf(x)\,dx=\frac{b-a}{2}\int_{-1}^{1}f\Big(\frac{a+b}{2}+\frac{b-a}{2}t\Big)\,dt.$$ 在标准公式中代入后，节点变为 $x_i=\frac{a+b}{2}+\frac{b-a}{2}t_i$，权重整体乘以 $\frac{b-a}{2}$，且 $\sum_iA_i^{(a,b)}=b-a$。若 $f\in C^{2n}[a,b]$，余项（真值减近似）为 $$R_n=\frac{(b-a)^{2n+1}(n!)^4}{(2n+1)[(2n)!]^3}f^{(2n)}(\xi),\qquad \xi\in(a,b).$$ 例如 $n=2$ 时 $R_2=\frac{(b-a)^5}{4320}f^{(4)}(\xi)$。$n$ 增大时误差依赖更高阶导数，光滑函数收敛极快；但若 $f^{(2n)}$ 很大或 $f$ 不光滑，固定 $n$ 未必有效，应把区间分段并在每段用低阶公式。

同一构造适用于非负权函数 $w$：公式 $$\int_a^bw(x)f(x)\,dx\approx\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_if(x_i)$$ 的节点取关于 $w$ 正交的 $p_n$ 的零点，权重 $A_i=\int_a^bw\ell_i$（对正权，Gauss 权重 $A_i>0$），代数精度仍为 $2n-1$；此时区间可以无限，有限端点可以带可积奇性，只要各阶矩 $\int_a^bw(x)|x|^k\,dx$ 有限。常见例子：Chebyshev 权 $w=(1-x^2)^{-1/2}$ 在 $[-1,1]$，节点 $\cos\frac{(2i-1)\pi}{2n}$，权重 $\frac{\pi}{n}$；Hermite 权 $w=e^{-x^2}$ 在 $\mathbb R$；Laguerre 权 $w=e^{-x}$ 在 $[0,\infty)$。若端点有代数奇性，也可用 Jacobi 权 $w=(1-x)^\alpha(1+x)^\beta$（$\alpha,\beta>-1$）把奇性吸收进权重。反之，若 $w$ 变号或矩不存在，正交多项式理论的标准结论不能直接套用，不能据此断言 $2n-1$ 的精度。
en: Let $w$ be continuous, nonnegative and not identically zero on $(a,b)$ (more generally, it suffices that $w\ge0$ and $w>0$ on a set of positive measure). Consider the quadrature rule $$\int_a^b w(x)f(x)\,dx\approx\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_if(x_i),$$ with distinct nodes $x_i$. If the rule is exact for every polynomial of degree at most $d$, take $$p(x)=\prod_{i=1}^{n}(x-x_i)^2.$$ Then $\deg p=2n$ and $p(x_i)=0$, so the right-hand side is $0$; but $p\ge0$ and vanishes only at finitely many points, while $w>0$ on a set of positive measure, so $\int_a^bw(x)p(x)\,dx>0$. This contradiction shows $d\le2n-1$: no $n$-point rule can have degree $2n$.

Assume the moments $\int_a^b w(x)x^k\,dx$ are finite, and let $\{p_k\}$ be the monic orthogonal polynomials with respect to $w$: $\deg p_k=k$ and $\int_a^bw p_kp_l=0$ for $k\ne l$; they are obtained from $1,x,x^2,\dots$ by Gram–Schmidt. For a positive weight, the $n$ zeros of $p_n$ are distinct and lie in $(a,b)$; take them as the nodes $x_i$. For any $f$ with $\deg f\le2n-1$, divide with remainder $$f(x)=q(x)p_n(x)+r(x),\qquad \deg q,\deg r\le n-1.$$ By orthogonality $\int_a^bw qp_n=0$, so $\int_a^bwf=\int_a^bwr$. Let $A_i=\int_a^bw(x)\ell_i(x)\,dx$, where $\ell_i$ are the Lagrange basis functions at the nodes. Since $r=\sum_ir(x_i)\ell_i$, we have $\sum_iA_ir(x_i)=\int_a^bwr$; and $p_n(x_i)=0$ gives $f(x_i)=r(x_i)$, hence $\sum_iA_if(x_i)=\int_a^bwf$. Thus the rule is exact for every $f$ of degree at most $2n-1$; combined with Step 1, $2n-1$ is the maximum. Conversely, if some $n$-point rule also attains $2n-1$, let $P(x)=\prod_i(x-x_i)$. For every $q$ of degree at most $n-1$, the polynomial $qP$ has degree at most $2n-1$ and vanishes at the nodes, so $\int_a^bw qP=0$. Hence $P$ is orthogonal to every polynomial of degree at most $n-1$, so $P$ is a constant multiple of $p_n$; since both are monic, $P=p_n$, and the nodes are exactly the zeros of $p_n$. Thus the node choice attaining the bound is unique up to ordering.

Take $[a,b]=[-1,1]$ and $w=1$. The orthogonal polynomials are the Legendre polynomials $P_n$, with $P_0=1$, $P_1=x$, the recurrence $$(n+1)P_{n+1}(x)=(2n+1)xP_n(x)-nP_{n-1}(x),\qquad P_n(1)=1.$$ Take the zeros $x_i$ of $P_n$ as nodes (monic normalization does not change the zeros). The Christoffel–Darboux identity gives $$\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{P_n(x)}{x-x_i}\,dx=\frac{2}{(1-x_i^2)P_n'(x_i)},$$ and since $\ell_i(x)=\frac{P_n(x)}{P_n'(x_i)(x-x_i)}$, the weights are $$A_i=\int_{-1}^{1}\ell_i(x)\,dx=\frac{2}{(1-x_i^2)[P_n'(x_i)]^2}.$$ Here we used $(1-x^2)P_n'(x)=n[P_{n-1}(x)-xP_n(x)]$, which at a zero becomes $(1-x_i^2)P_n'(x_i)=nP_{n-1}(x_i)$. Because $x_i\in(-1,1)$, $1-x_i^2>0$ and $[P_n'(x_i)]^2>0$, so $A_i>0$; and since the constant $1$ is integrated exactly, $\sum_iA_i=\int_{-1}^1 1\,dx=2$.

The low-order rules can be checked directly: for $n=1$, $P_1=x$, the node is $0$ and $A_1=\frac{2}{1\cdot1}=2$, the midpoint rule; for $n=2$, $P_2=\frac12(3x^2-1)$, the nodes are $\pm\frac1{\sqrt3}$, $P_2'=3x$, and $A_i=\frac{2}{(1-\frac13)\cdot3}=1$; for $n=3$, $P_3=\frac12(5x^3-3x)$, the nodes are $0,\pm\sqrt{\frac35}$, with weights $\frac89,\frac59,\frac59$. Accuracy check: for $n=2$ and $x^2$, $\sum_iA_ix_i^2=2\cdot\frac13=\frac23=\int_{-1}^1x^2dx$, while for $x^4$, $\sum_iA_ix_i^4=2\cdot\frac19=\frac29\ne\frac25$, so the degree is exactly $2n-1=3$. For $n=3$ and $x^4$, $2\cdot\frac59\cdot\frac{9}{25}=\frac25$, consistent with the integral because $4\le2n-1=5$.

For a general interval $[a,b]$, set $$x=\frac{a+b}{2}+\frac{b-a}{2}t,\qquad t\in[-1,1],\qquad dx=\frac{b-a}{2}\,dt.$$ Then $$\int_a^bf(x)\,dx=\frac{b-a}{2}\int_{-1}^{1}f\Big(\frac{a+b}{2}+\frac{b-a}{2}t\Big)\,dt.$$ After substitution into the standard rule, the nodes become $x_i=\frac{a+b}{2}+\frac{b-a}{2}t_i$, all weights are multiplied by $\frac{b-a}{2}$, and $\sum_iA_i^{(a,b)}=b-a$. If $f\in C^{2n}[a,b]$, the remainder (true value minus approximation) is $$R_n=\frac{(b-a)^{2n+1}(n!)^4}{(2n+1)[(2n)!]^3}f^{(2n)}(\xi),\qquad \xi\in(a,b).$$ For example, for $n=2$, $R_2=\frac{(b-a)^5}{4320}f^{(4)}(\xi)$. As $n$ grows the error involves higher derivatives, so smooth integrands converge extremely fast; but if $f^{(2n)}$ is large or $f$ is not smooth, a fixed $n$ may be ineffective, and one should subdivide the interval and use a low-order rule on each piece.

The same construction applies to a nonnegative weight function $w$: the rule $$\int_a^bw(x)f(x)\,dx\approx\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_if(x_i)$$ has nodes at the zeros of the orthogonal polynomial $p_n$ with respect to $w$, weights $A_i=\int_a^bw\ell_i$ (which are positive for a positive weight), and degree of precision $2n-1$; the interval may be infinite, and finite endpoints may carry integrable singularities, provided the moments $\int_a^bw(x)|x|^k\,dx$ are finite. Common examples: the Chebyshev weight $w=(1-x^2)^{-1/2}$ on $[-1,1]$, with nodes $\cos\frac{(2i-1)\pi}{2n}$ and weights $\frac{\pi}{n}$; the Hermite weight $w=e^{-x^2}$ on $\mathbb R$; and the Laguerre weight $w=e^{-x}$ on $[0,\infty)$. For algebraic endpoint singularities one may also use the Jacobi weight $w=(1-x)^\alpha(1+x)^\beta$ with $\alpha,\beta>-1$, which absorbs the singularity into the weight. Conversely, if $w$ changes sign or its moments fail to exist, the standard orthogonal-polynomial theory does not apply directly, and the $2n-1$ conclusion cannot be asserted.
